keyRules: In the open category, the maximum height is 120 m, measured as the distance to the closest point on the earth’s surface — not just straight down, so near a slope the ground beside you may also count. Within 50 m of a tall artificial obstacle (over 105 m), the person responsible for the obstacle can apply for permission to fly up to 15 m above the obstacle’s height.

You must register as a drone operator if your drone weighs 250 g or more (or can transfer more than 80 J of kinetic energy in a collision) — this applies even to toys. Under 250 g, registration is still required if the drone has a sensor able to capture personal data, unless it counts as a toy under the EU Toy Safety Directive. Pilot training/certificate requirements are separate and depend on the drone’s class and subcategory.

In Norway, the age limit for flying on your own is 16. Exceptions apply to C0 drones classified as toys and to privately built drones under 250 g with a maximum speed below 19 m/s. If you are under 16, you may fly under the direct supervision of a remote pilot who is at least 16 and holds a valid certificate of competence.
EU registration from your home country is valid—no new Norwegian registration is required
Liability insurance is normally required for weights of 250 g or more (no requirement for weights under 250 g in the open category)

Tower clearance is required to fly within 5 km of an airport — contact the air traffic service by phone or email, or apply via the Ninox Drone app (Avinor) where it is in use. The app is not a requirement.

Central Oslo (R102) is a permanent restricted area — flying requires prior permission from Luftfartstilsynet (apply via Altinn or postmottak@caa.no, approx. two weeks’ processing time, subject to a fee). The police normally do not grant permission on New Year’s Eve/Day, 17 May, the opening day of the Storting or 10 December.
Remote Identification (Remote ID) is required for C1–C3-class drones
Always check protected areas and national parks separately
importantNotes: Foreign pilots with cameras or sensors: Notify the NSM (National Security Authority) before flying
Svalbard has its own very strict rules—see the Governor’s website
Norway fully complies with the EASA Open Category (Open Category A1/A2/A3)
